subject: BrightCom EU launch — third-party scan & mitigation plan
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: BrightCom EU launch — third-party scan & mitigation plan

Team,

BrightCom is pushing to launch their EU marketing site next week. They just shared a third-party scan (see attachment) and asked for an inventory and mitigation plan specifically for marketing pixels and tag vendors that may process EU personal data. Olivia says their legal team will want evidence for SCCs and a short DPIA write-up for any vendor classified as 'high risk'.

Can Mina and Neha take point on: 1) confirming which vendors we send analytics/telemetry to (pixel & server calls); 2) whether any of those require SCCs or HIPAA considerations; 3) a short mitigation plan per vendor (consent gating, data minimization, hashing, server-side proxying). I've attached our public privacy policy for reference.

Attachments: [thirdparty-scan-report-20260928.pdf (pdf)], [privacy-policy-redwood-inference-20260901.pdf (pdf)]

Thanks,
Vivek
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: BrightCom EU launch — third-party scan & mitigation plan

Hi Olivia,

Thanks for the scan — I pulled this into our security queue and looped in Mina and Neha from Privacy & Compliance. We're preparing a concise vendor inventory and mitigation plan. Expect a first pass by EOD PST today.

To expedite, can you confirm whether you consider any of the following 'high risk' for BrightCom: health-related form captures, user identifiers tied to CRM records, or any pixel that forwards email/phone in query strings? Also, do you have a preferred SCC template or are you fine with our standard EU SCCs? (We can supply both.)

Quick attachments: [cookie_inventory_brightcom_v1.csv (csv) — internal draft]

Regards,
Vivek

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@brightcom.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T20:45:00+01:00
Subject: Re: BrightCom EU launch — third-party scan & mitigation plan

Thanks Vivek — quick answers:
- BrightCom considers form captures that include "health_status" as high risk (we tag those pages).
- We do send hashed email to our personalization vendor for lookups.
- Preferred SCCs: our legal team prefers the updated EU SCCs; happy to review yours.

Helpful if you can call out any pixels that are non-essential for EU visitors and provide a recommended gating approach (consent banner + reject option). Also, can your privacy policy excerpt show how you rely on SCCs or other transfer mechanism? We need screenshots for our DPIA.

Olivia
Director, Privacy & Compliance
BrightCom

---
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@brightcom.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: BrightCom EU launch — third-party scan & mitigation plan

Hi Olivia,

Attached is a concise deliverable addressing your asks:
1) Inventory: attached CSV lists all detected third-party endpoints, purpose, data categories, and whether calls originate from client-side pixels or server-side SDKs.
2) High-risk flags: rows marked "HR" identify vendors processing form-derived health indicators or hashed identifiers.
3) Mitigation plan: per-vendor recommendations — consent gating (CCPA/GDPR opt-in), move to server-side proxying for hashed identifiers, strip email fragments in query strings, and minimize retention.
4) DPIA evidence: we included a screenshot of our consent banner (see screenshot) and a short paragraph you can paste into your DPIA describing our SCC adoption and data-flow boundaries.

Attachments included:
- cookie_inventory_brightcom_v1.csv (csv)
- screenshot-consent-banner.png (png)
- thirdparty-scan-report-20260928.pdf (pdf)
- privacy-policy-redwood-inference-20260901.pdf (pdf)

Notes:
- Vendors flagged HR: PersonalizePro (hashed-email lookups), AdReach (client-side audience syncs), HealthFormAnalytics (form payload analysis). For PersonalizePro we recommend server-side hash matching via our proxy (reduces exposure of raw email hashes) and an SCC addendum; AdReach should be optional for EU visitors behind a consent reject; HealthFormAnalytics requires a Data Processing Addendum plus documented legal basis — we'll escalate to legal if BrightCom intends to keep it active for EU.

Let me know if you want a short (1-page) DPIA paragraph we can drop into your template; we can also produce signed SCCs and DPA attachments if you send contacts.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Privacy Manager
Redwood Inference
